newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end higher on global trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end higher on global trend.

text.p: ** Indian gold 24 carat ends Thursday 10 rupees higher at 4,690 rupees per 10 gramme but off the day's opening 4,700 rupees as demand resistance capped early gains towards close.
** Gold biscuits (116.50 gramme each) close 200 rupees higher at 54,900 rupees per piece but off the opening 55,000 rupees.
** Silver (.999) ends 40 rupees higher at 7,340 rupees per kg on limited supplies -- uptrend in world market helps prices bounce back.
Gold prices opened Thursday higher on overnight gains in the world market but lower than expected seasonal buying trimmed early gains towards the close, dealers said.
Gold 24 carat closed 10 rupees higher from the previous close at 4,690 rupees per 10 gramme but 10 rupees down from the opening level of 4,700 rupees, they said.
Gold was down 20 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
"Market rumours that the government may allow free import of gold in the approaching Exim (export-import) policy also softened sentiments towards the close," one dealer said.

Prices of gold biscuits higher at 54,900 rupees per piece against the previous close of 54,700 rupees but down from the opening level of 55,000 rupees. They were down 300 rupees per piece on Wednesday.

Silver (.999) closed 40 rupees higher at 7,340 rupees per kg as overnight gains in the world market helped local prices bounce back, while industrial support checked the fall in prices. Silver was down 90 rupees per kg on Wednesday.
The Bombay bullion market is closed on March 28 for Good Friday. (Conversion $1=35.89 rupees)
